## Destination

Every open question in the 2026-07 fleet-audit remediation programme is **decided and implemented** — on `main`, CI green, and where the change is a contract, carrying a gate that goes red if it regresses. The map is finished when **no issue carrying `wayfinder:247` remains open**.

## Notes

<!-- STANDING RULES ONLY. Session narrative goes in a comment on this issue, never here.
     GitHub caps this body at 262,144 bytes and the whole thing is loaded at the start of every
     session, so the budget is tighter than the ceiling: keep the body under 150 KB and this
     section under 16 KB. Check it as part of the harvest, not when an edit fails:
       gh issue view 247 -R encryption4all/postguard --json body -q .body | wc -c
     A finding earns a place here by holding for the third time; promote it then, and say in the
     session note that you did. Everything else stays in the comment where it was written. -->

**Domain.** Nine repos across two orgs implementing PostGuard: IBE/IBS crypto (`pg-core`), a PKG service, C ABI + .NET bindings, a Rust file-transfer service (cryptify), a JS SDK monorepo with three email clients, an e2e harness, and Terraform ops. The organising insight from the July 2026 audit (11 repos, code review + a year of failure archaeology) is that the dominant failure class is **cross-repo contract drift** — contracts existed only as convention, so they drifted silently ~40 times a year. The strategy is: remove seams where possible, and make the surviving ones executable. **Prose specs are explicitly out** — fixtures and CI gates are the spec.

**This map carries execution, not just decisions.** Wayfinder normally stops at the decision; this effort deliberately overrides that. A ticket is done when the thing is built, not when the approach is chosen.

**Done bar.** Merged to `main` with CI green, and a gate that fails on regression where the ticket touches a contract. Publishing a release and deploying to prod are explicitly *not* required to close a ticket — with one deliberate exception, `#348`, whose deliverable is a published advisory. For the ops repo, "merged" means merged *and applied*, since Terraform's merge is its deploy.

**Membership is the `wayfinder:247` label, and so is the frontier.** The tree hit GitHub's hard cap of 100 sub-issues on 2026-09-02, which silently stopped the map accepting new work and made four charted tickets invisible ([#396](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/396)). The label is now the membership record — on every member, open **and** closed, so a reopened ticket returns to the frontier — and the parent/child links are UI convenience. **Unwire a child when you close it**, in the same step as the resolution comment and the index entry; the cap counts closed children too, and this map filled 100 slots in five weeks. Run the query; do not read a list, and do not count leaves from a number written here:

```bash
# every open member, across all four repos
for r in encryption4all/postguard encryption4all/postguard-js \
         encryption4all/postguard-e2e privacybydesign/postguard-ops; do
  gh issue list -R "$r" --label wayfinder:247 --state open --limit 200 \
    --json number,title,assignees --jq ".[] | \"$r#\(.number) \(.assignees|length) \(.title)\""
done
```

The frontier is the open, unblocked, **unassigned** members. This replaced a `subIssues` walk that only ever returned depth-1 children, so takeable leaves sitting inside umbrellas never appeared in it. Umbrellas are wired `blocked by` their own open children and drop off the frontier the moment those close — check them for the open-but-done shape rather than waiting to trip over it. **A closed wired blocker is not the only blocker**: no dependency edge models a release pipeline, an unpublished artifact, or "this PR before that one", so a ticket can read takeable and not be. Where that is true it is said on the ticket.

**Division of labour.** dobby (the `dobby-coder` GitHub App) writes the code and tests but **cannot push `.github/workflows/*.yml`** — it lacks `workflows: write`, so it leaves the YAML in a comment for a maintainer to apply. Both halves of that handover fail, in two distinct ways: a patch **never posted** (`#324` — check the URL it is claimed to be at), and a patch **posted correctly and never applied** (`#272`, and again on `postguard-e2e` — checking the URL passes, only reading the file catches it). `postguard` and `postguard-js` machine-read their own workflows (`pg-core/tests/ci_wiring.rs`, `packages/pg-js/tests/ci-wiring.test.ts`), so an unapplied patch there reds a suite; `delivery.yml` and all of `postguard-e2e` are unguarded. **A workflow handover is verified by reading the file on `main` and then by reading the step's output in a run on `main`** — a green PR is evidence about the PR, and a green wiring test is evidence about jobs and contexts. Neither is evidence a step landed. `privacybydesign/postguard-ops` **has no coding agent at all** — zero `dobby-coder` PRs in its history — so its tickets can never be dispatched however well written.

**Verify before you build — and the thing to re-read is rarely the source file.** Read the ticket's target at `origin/main` (`git show origin/main:<path>`), never the working tree. Then extend the same suspicion to every other kind of premise, because each of these has cost this map at least one cycle: a ticket's **line numbers** (stale, and once inverted); its **citations** (closing an issue is exactly what makes a reference to it wrong); its **dates** (a ticket can instruct an agent to write a stale date onto the one line recording currency); its **closed sets** (an allowlist has to be checked against every emitter, not against the reader — there are five, and checking two and inferring three is how `pg-cli` and `dotnet` were nearly dropped); its **cost estimates** (one was inverted by four minutes of running the formatter); and its **premises against its own siblings**, which keep moving while it waits, and not monotonically — one merge made `#370` more dispatchable and less, at once. A PR is authoritative about its own closes, so ask it rather than inferring from timing: `gh api graphql -f query='{repository(owner:"O",name:"R"){pullRequest(number:N){closingIssuesReferences(first:10){nodes{number}}}}}'`.

**An agent's self-report is unreliable in both directions, and silence carries no information.** Four shapes, all observed: a **handover reported that never happened** (`#324`); **"CI is green"** three seconds after the push that started the runs, true of the previous sha (`#343`); **"no changes were made"** over a complete, green, 40-check branch, with an invitation to re-dispatch that would have discarded it (`#362`, then `#364`); and a **`/dobby` on a pull request**, which routes to the *review* pipeline and blocks nothing, so the PR merges as written (`#384`). Read the branch and the checks of the sha the PR points at now — never the narration. Dispatch acknowledgement latency is **bimodal** (seconds when dobby is free, unbounded when rate-limited) and its **absence means nothing at all**: it cannot distinguish *not started* from *never arrived*. **Never re-fire on silence** — ask the queue; a second `/dobby` buys a duplicate, not a retry. And **verify a verification before trusting it**: a watcher written to poll for acks reported clean negatives because its `gh` calls were failing into `|| echo 0`.

**Harvest owns more than reading a label, and it runs at both ends of a session.** **Harvest by label, not by state** — a *closed* ticket still carrying `wayfinder:in-flight` is an unfinished harvest, and that has been the rule rather than the anomaly. **Clearing the mark is not the harvest**; a cleared mark is indistinguishable from a finished one. **A closed dispatch ticket is not a finished one** — diff what the PR touched against what the ticket asked for, because a trailer closes an issue on the strength of a branch nobody read. Three free commands stand between a finished branch and a review queue and none is visible to any query: **un-draft** (`gh pr ready` — four consecutive dobby dispatches delivered complete green work and lost only the finalize step), **re-run a flake**, and **check the release PRs**. Re-measure the mid-flight set every time rather than carrying the previous session's table forward — this map has twice described a PR as awaiting review that had merged days earlier, and once counted a PR that had been **superseded** six weeks before. **An open-PR count cannot tell a stalled review from a dead PR.** An in-flight mark older than a day with no branch is failed, not pending; an in-flight mark outside every frontier query is a claim nobody will collect — wire the ticket in or drop the mark.

**The dispatch gate, and the five questions it does not ask.** The gate is in the skill; what this map has added is what slips past it. **Gate 1 is settled by reading the code the ticket points at, not by reading the ticket** — a body can be specific, confident and well-written and still describe a move the tree does not offer. Ask **"what artifact does this ticket write, and can the agent write that kind of artifact"** *before* reading the body: a workflow file, an org-wide App installation, and edits to someone else's PR branch are all gate-5 rejects knowable from the deliverable's path or verb. Check a batch for **file collisions**, which no gate question asks — two dispatches against one file is a bad merge waiting to happen, and wiring `blocked by` at charting time for that reason alone is good practice. Check that a ticket's own tests are **reachable under its own scope fence**. Answer gate 3 by reading the target repo's **test config**, never by guessing which directory gates. And expect a **pre-flight amendment**: a dispatch body is checked against the code it names and not against the code that names it, so grep the *identifier* rather than re-reading the ticket's line numbers. Amendments demonstrably work — the tickets that need none are the ones a previous wayfinder session wrote to the gate, and whose premises were measurements rather than readings. Roughly seven in eight swept candidates fail, almost always on gate 1: **the frontier's remaining `wayfinder:task` tickets are mostly grilling tickets wearing task labels.** Relabel when you take one.

**The fail-open family: for every new gate or signal, ask what it reports when its subject is absent rather than wrong.** Instances, all real: a required check with a `paths` filter and nothing to report (`#299`); a metric that drops what it cannot parse, so an empty panel reads as a confident zero (`#371`); a `wayfinder:in-flight` query against a repo where the label was never created; an in-flight query against a repo with no coding agent; `pnpm --filter` skipping a package with no `lint` script, silently, ten lines below the guard that fixes exactly that (`examples.yml`); `alloy validate` exiting 0 on an empty endpoint URL; and the inversion — a check with something real to say and **no permission to say it**, where four days of *awaiting approval* is indistinguishable from four days of *nothing wrong* (`#394`). Two habits: **test the checker against a known-bad input before believing its pass**, and **a rationale written into a code comment is a claim like any other**.

**Reaching `main` is roughly half the distance to a user.** The other half is a release PR that arrives **pre-gated** — `check-runs: 0`, `action_required`, `BLOCKED` — and waits on a human who is never notified. The discriminator is the *actor*: `app/github-actions` (what `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` makes release-plz) gets zero check-runs where `rubenhensen` and `app/dobby-coder` get dozens. It is **one approval per sha**, and a release PR re-shas whenever `main` moves under it, so the busier `main` is the further the release falls behind — a treadmill, not a checkpoint. It has stranded a security fix on `main` and on no registry three times. [#334](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/334) owns this. Not every zero-runs PR is that gate — `CONFLICTING` looks identical through `gh pr checks`. **Check the release PRs at every harvest**, because an empty in-flight sweep now reads as *done* while releases sit still. Downstream, **a caret resolves a fix; it does not require one**, and a pre-1.0 caret cannot cross a minor boundary — consumers pinned `^0.5.x` can never resolve a `0.6.x` fix, which is the one case `cargo audit`/`npm audit` cannot resolve for a consumer. And **check that a fix reaches the code path before calling something either a gap or a vulnerability** — it has pointed both ways here.

**Measure registries and pipelines together, and believe the pipeline first.** A registry read lags a publish and fails in the exact shape of one that never happened: for **2m08s** after `@e4a/pg-js@2.6.0` published, `dist-tags.latest` was stale, `GET /<pkg>/<version>` **404'd**, `time.modified` read three weeks old, and cache-busting changed none of it — the JSON endpoint is no better than `npm view`, both read one lagging document, and no registry field distinguishes *not yet* from *never*. **The pipeline log is the authority; the registry only confirms.** One `gh api .../jobs` call separates *the publish failed* from *it has not run yet* from *it landed and the registry lags*, and only the first is a finding. crates.io's API needs a `User-Agent` or its 404 looks like a crate never published.

**Repo posture: admin merges are the normal path here, deliberately.** `dobby-coder` cannot self-approve and neither can a maintainer authoring their own PR. Classic protection keeps `enforce_admins: false`, so `--admin` still walks past the *review* requirement — but a separate ruleset `main: required checks` with `bypass_actors: []` means it **cannot** walk past a red or *absent* gate. `postguard-js` has the same posture via a ruleset split. **`bypass_actors` is ruleset-level, not per-rule** — that is why differential enforcement needs two objects, and why re-adding one actor to the wrong ruleset silently makes 20 contexts advisory again. This repo's required-context registry is asserted by the `ruleset-drift` job against the pins in `ci_wiring.rs`; `postguard-js`'s 20 are still unguarded ([#331](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/331)). Both repos **squash-merge**, so `git merge-base --is-ancestor` reports *not on main* for work that plainly is — read the squash commit on `main`, not the PR's head sha.

**History-preserving imports silently close issues here.** `ba380a14` closed live issue [#146](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/146) via an imported commit's `Closes encryption4all/postguard-website#146`, resolved against *this* repo's numbering. Nothing warned. Audit closing keywords before and after any such merge; the guard is [postguard-js#139](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/139). Measure the hazard rather than fearing it — `postguard-dotnet`'s nine keywords all target already-closed items, which made a history-preserving import the cheap option there. And when retiring a repo, **turn its release automation off first**: `release-plz-pr` re-created cryptify's superseded release PR one minute after it was closed. Automation off and README finalized in one PR, then close the PRs, then transfer, then archive.

**Repo consolidation is finished.** All five source repos — the four app repos plus `cryptify` — are transferred and archived as of 2026-08-09 ([#294](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/294)), and the 62 issues stranded in archived read-only repos are moved. Nothing in the fleet is left half-moved.

**Skills.** `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` for the `wayfinder:grilling` tickets; `/prototype` for `wayfinder:prototype`. Repo-durable knowledge lives in root `CLAUDE.md` — read it before touching any gate, and update it in the same PR when a ticket teaches something lasting. It carries its own 4,000-byte budget with a test behind it; do not relieve pressure here by spending it there.

     NOT yet standing rules in Notes. One line each, with a count of how many tickets have hit it.
     On the third hit, promote it into Notes and delete the line here; Notes is at its own 16,000-byte
     budget, so a promotion has to evict something rather than grow it. An instance of a rule ALREADY
     in Notes does not belong here at all — it changes nothing a session does. Verified 2026-09-22
     against 31 entries and their full tickets: this genre is rare, so if this section is filling up,
     check that its lines are not restatements of Notes rules. -->

- **A timeout is not a cost.** Pricing a job at its failure budget rather than measuring a passing run. (1 — #416)
- **Read the passing log, not only the failing one.** The diagnostic a ticket asks to be built often already ships in every green run. (1 — #416)
- **"Reuse the script X extracts" is a claim about X.** A dependency wired from a sibling's title rather than its interface. (1 — #416)
- **`gh issue list --label` lags the label write**, by enough to report a mark just cleared — confirm a label edit with `gh issue view`, not the search index. (1 — #412)
- **A zero-runs PR is not always #334's gate.** `CONFLICTING` looks identical through `gh pr checks`: GitHub will not run `pull_request` workflows it cannot build a merge commit for. (1 — #394)
- **Gate 4 cuts both ways — the comments are the reader's whole world too.** #399 was resolved twice because a session read the issue body and not its comments. (1 — #399)

Append-only enforced twice — a ledger plus a merge-base diff that also freezes the ledger. Proven by a real tamper PR.
- [cryptify/dev.Dockerfile is not workspace-aware, so every dev consumer still builds from the archived repo](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/325) — **fixed**: repo root as context, every member copied in both stages. Durable: a guard's exemption clause is where the next instance hides — prove the guard reds on the pre-fix tree before believing a list entry did anything.
- [store: restore sessions on boot; chunk replay and resume survive restart](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/303) — **live**: `Store::restore_sessions` rebuilds the map at construction. Two wall-clock deadlines decide whether a row returns — `last_active_at + idle_ttl` and the 14-day `expires` — and the idle window keeps running while the process is down.
- [compat: bump-manifest.mjs moves the manifest but not the fixtures' pg-js pin](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-e2e/issues/36) — **fixed** in the bumper, not the gate — its strictness was the point. `COUPLED_PINS` names pins that must follow a manifest entry; fixtures' `@e4a/pg-wasm` is deliberately uncoupled so it ages against the corpus. Pins are written before the manifest.
- [e2e: provision business-db from real postguard-business migrations](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/237) — **fixed**: `business-schema-source` fetches postguard-business's `drizzle/migrations` and applies them before seeding data. The fork was decided by a tooling constraint: the alternative needed an `e2e.yml` edit the App cannot push.
- [e2e: keyshare-backed disclosure flow (test scheme + keyshare server)](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/238) — **fixed**: `TestKeyshareDisclosureFlow` sits beside existing flows. What it asserts is the reusable part — a `ProofStatusValid`-only check would pass over a credential the holder can prove alone, so it also asserts the attribute, keyshare calls and a PIN prompt.
- [version sweep to CI: support-matrix of published SDKs vs candidate servers, nightly and pre-deploy, with decrypt legs](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-e2e/issues/21) — **live**, the deploy-time backstop to the PR-time wire gate. The matrix is data in `src/matrix.mjs`, not a workflow `matrix:` block, so nightly, pre-deploy and hand sweeps cover one set. Two legs: `wire`, `decrypt`.
- [tb-addon's formatting is enforced only by a git hook, so `--no-verify` lands unformatted](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/324) — **fixed**: one `Prettier (format check)` step inside `tb-addon.yml`'s existing `build` job — a step rather than a job, so it reports under the already-required `Build & test` and needs no ruleset change. It checks wider than the hook's globs.
- [decide: the `developers` team bypasses all 20 required checks on `postguard-js`'s `main` ruleset](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/317) — **split it, #299-style**: ruleset `main` keeps the 1-review rule and the `developers` bypass; a new `main: required checks` (`bypass_actors: []`) holds the 20 contexts. 10 of the last 12 merges had 0 approvals.
- [external compatibility: never break a consumer we don't control](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/248) — umbrella, **all five children done**: `COMPATIBILITY.md`, `cargo-semver-checks`, the JS public-API snapshot gate, `PublicApiAnalyzers` on .NET, and the deploy-time version sweep. Every one replaced a promise with something that fails. Live descendants: #327, #268.
- [spike: assert the required-context list itself, not just the workflow wiring](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/318) — **the premise was wrong and the gate was free** — both repos are public, so `rules/branches/{branch}` answers 200 to the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` at every permission level, across repositories. Deliberately not required, no `schedule:`. Gap: #331/#332.
- [backlog: container format 3 — authenticate preamble+header (AAD + signature binding), format number = wire value](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/258) — **designed, not built**, graduating #339, #340, #341. No primitive changes; what changes is which bytes the crypto covers. Rule: each element authenticated over everything preceding it. Version stays at bytes 4..6.
- [Chunk sizes should be configured server-side and fetched by clients](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/147) — **decided**: only `upload_chunk` is a seam — cryptify serves a global `max_chunk_size_bytes` on the init 200 body, absent field falling back to `5_000_000`. The durable half is why the other three are not seams. Split into #343 and postguard-js#231.
- [pg-core: canonical identity normalization (email lowercase, E.164 phone) with test vectors, exported via wasm/ffi](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/250) — **live**: `identity.rs` carries `canonicalize`/`is_canonical` and `RULES`. The canonical form is Yivi's. Canonicalization is a **coarsening of equality**: it can only merge identities, never split a matching pair.
- [pg-core: name the version constants after their wire values (VERSION_V3 = 2 is a trap)](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/339) — **shipped**, the **first dispatch**. `VERSION_0/_1/_2` canonical, `VERSION_V1/V2/V3` kept as `#[deprecated]` aliases, which stopped a naming fix costing pg-core a major. `pg-compat` builds against *published* pg-core, so it must keep the old names.
- [cryptify: serve the configured max upload-chunk size on POST /fileupload/init](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/343) — **shipped**, the **second dispatch**. `max_chunk_size_bytes` rides the init 200 body from `config.chunk_size()` — the same accessor the enforcement check reads, so served and enforced cannot disagree. The gate is a round trip at a non-default 1 MiB.
- [pg-compat cannot pin two same-minor pg-core versions, so the documented support-window recipe fails](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/327) — **the fork dissolved on measurement**: the pg-core window is per *line*, so it never asks for two same-minor pins and #268's row move is a replacement. Root cause: nothing notices when a version publishes (#353).
- [the wire-compat gate is blind to identity canonicalization: every sample value is already canonical](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/336) — **decided: the fixture goes in both sender policies**; the recipient half was factually wrong — no reader derives from a recipient policy. `.canonical()` is load-bearing for what a recipient is *shown*, not what is *derived*. #355.
- [pg-core: bind the public signing policy into the AEAD plaintext, so a swapped h_sig_ext is rejected](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/347) — **shipped**, the **third dispatch**: a second copy of the canonicalized public signing policy rides inside the AEAD. It binds to the DEM key, not the sender's signing key, so a co-recipient is not stopped — residual in #338/#340.
- [Unsealer.pub_id is documented "verified" but is unbound until unseal, so a display-before-decrypt client bypasses #347's check](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/350) — **the audit was the answer**: two shipped consumers, not a latent trap — the website's pre-scan `Ready` block and cryptify. A relay is not a reader. #357, #358, postguard-js#232.
- [backlog: envelope format 2 — self-describing part, fix double-base64](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/259) — **decided, not built; the ticket dissolved — there is no envelope format 2.** It bundled an outer-layer detection change with an inner-MIME encoding one. Detection becomes a union (preamble OR filename OR uuid-link), needing no wire format. Five children.
- [cryptify trusts the container's unbound sender for the notification email and the default-tier quota key](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/358) — **cryptify gets its own checkpoint at upload time.** Challenge-response verified against the identity derived from the container's own header. Durable: never give an intermediary a credential that mints keys; give it a statement.
- [pg-compat: move the crates.io reader pin to 0.6.3, and guard the one-pin-per-minor-line constraint](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/352) — **shipped**, the **fourth dispatch**: pin moved `=0.6.1` → `=0.6.3` and `no_two_pinned_readers_share_a_minor_line` now enforces the constraint. It is cargo's resolver rule, not semver's — cargo unifies on the **major** alone.
- [COMPATIBILITY.md: envelope detection never expires, and two live gates are still described as planned](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/360) — **shipped**. Envelope detection now falls under the read-access guarantee, so the `postguard.encrypted` name is kept forever. The move mattered more than the wording: a guarantee must live beside the process that could revoke it.
- [the download page shows a verified checkmark next to an unverified sender, before decryption](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/232) — **shipped**: the green checkmark is gone and the hedged address stays — what asserted something false was the tick, not the address. Claimed-vs-verified now lives in the SDK's own types, so a second consumer cannot repeat it.
- [observability: scrape pkg and cryptify Prometheus metrics; minimal dashboard and alerts](https://github.com/privacybydesign/postguard-ops/issues/64) — **decided and split**, and the ticket would have defeated its own purpose as written: pg-js 1.x sends no `X-POSTGUARD-CLIENT-VERSION` and the middleware has no `unknown` bucket, so `postguard_clients` reports zero 1.x traffic forever.
- [fixtures: give the wire-compat sample set a non-canonical sender identity, and make pg-compat assert the sender policy](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/355) — **shipped**, the **sixth dispatch**: `SENDER` is now `" Sender@Sample.TEST "` and both policies carry a non-canonical vector, because a fixture on one leaves the other blind. Both reverts shown red.
- [pg-core, pg-wasm: a challenge-signature API for proving possession of a signing key](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/362) — **shipped**: `pg_core::challenge` with `sign_challenge`/`verify_challenge`. The domain separator is applied inside the functions, not passed in, so a verifier cannot get a valid `h_sig_ext` from a header dressed as a challenge.
- [cryptify: canonicalize the default-tier accounting key, so one identity cannot mint unlimited quota buckets](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/363) — **shipped**, `#358`'s quota half: `get_usage` and `record_upload` share one `accounting_key` helper, so check and accrual cannot disagree, and the no-tenant branch canonicalizes.
- [the envelope gate has no armored-body fixture, so deleting armor support turns nothing red](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/235) — **shipped.** Measured first: delete both armor readers and the archival suite still reports `13 passed`. The fixture could not be hand-written — HEAD cannot produce armor — so the generator calls a published old sender.
- [fixtures: the corpus needs an expected-failure class, for a tampered-sender container](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-e2e/issues/43) — **designed; the premise moved before its four questions could be answered** — `#347`'s check only fires on containers sealed at 0.6.4+, and every corpus set predates it, so there was nothing to tamper with. Graduated e2e#47, e2e#48.
- [the pre-decrypt sender identity is documented as verified, and it is only claimed](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/357) — **shipped.** Four doc sites, not the three the ticket named, and the type-level doc took the imperative form. The ticket's line numbers were stale and one pair was **inverted** — harmless only because the text was identical.
- [no reader row on any registry has a currency check, so the support window goes stale silently](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/353) — **decided and split three ways.** The gap was never *nothing watches*: `compat-bump.yml`'s 05:00 cron already tracks three of the four packages, so the whole missing piece is one crates.io backend. #378, #379, e2e#50.
- [cryptify: mint an upload challenge and verify it at finalize, reducing to a SenderClaim](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/364) — **shipped**, `#358`'s checked half: `upload_finalize` reduces `X-PostGuard-Proof` to a `SenderClaim`. The migration is `pragma_table_info`-driven — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` would have been a silent no-op on every deployed database.
- [fixtures: a pg-core 0.6.4 writer set, and the schema-3 bump that lets a negative case exist](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-e2e/issues/47) — **shipped.** The corpus's first set from the `pub_pol` era; a **second writer crate** rather than a third pin, since a same-minor pin cannot sit beside 0.6.1. `meta.json` goes to schema 3, and the version number *is* the deliverable.
- [Signed attributes get lost](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/199) — **the Outlook half was done; Thunderbird was never in scope until consolidation put it there.** A deferral can expire the same way a premise does — *out of scope for this repo* was true when written and false once the repos merged. js#264, js#265.
- [pg-js: answer cryptify's upload challenge so the sender identity is proven, not claimed](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/239) — **shipped**, closing the sender-authenticity chain — until this merged no client could satisfy `#364`'s verifier, so `Proven` was unreachable. `resumeUpload` rehydrates without the challenge, so a resumed session finalizes unproven.
- [pg-pkg drops header-less requests, so 'no 1.x traffic' is unfalsifiable](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/371) — **the diagnosis was right and the remedy did not follow from it.** There is no discriminator — 1.11.0 and 2.4.0 request an identical route set — so the fix converts a false green light into a permanent red one. #381, #382.
- [fixtures: the tampered-sender expected-failure class, and the reader table that gives it teeth](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-e2e/issues/48) — **shipped**: three swapped-signature containers and a `rejectsTampered` table. **A default chosen by sorting is a default any addition can capture** — `-tampered` sorted after `0.6.4` and silently took the sweep's key universe.
- [no test pins buildSignAttributes' combined flow, so #199's bug could return silently](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/265) — **shipped.** Six cases through `setSignPrefills`, with both failure shapes shown red against different sets — only test 4 catches the *drop* shape `#199` reported. An untestable claim and an out-of-scope claim look identical from outside.
- [may an unauthenticated caller learn cryptify's default-tier upload limits?](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/344) — **yes, and cryptify becomes the single authority**: a new unauthenticated `GET /limits`, default tier only, byte-identical for every caller. Three premises were wrong — `/usage` never served these numbers, and the limits are consts, not config.
- [COMPATIBILITY.md: drop the nuget row from the Reader list](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/378) — **shipped.** `E4A.PostGuard` is producer-only, so a reader gate would have nothing to call. The durable half is the distinction between two lists: the support window says what is supported, the reader list says what can read. Supersedes #268 by name.
- [cryptify: split the notification email into attributed and neutral renderings](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/365) — **shipped**: `email_attributed.{html,txt}` beside the neutral pair, the render path restructured around the **claim** rather than the template. The kill switch is a downgrade applied after the claim resolves, so it can only take attribution away.
- [pg-pkg: postguard_clients drops every unidentified request](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/381) — **shipped, minus one decision that was made and never applied.** A `/dobby` in a **pull request** comment routes to the *review* pipeline, so a change request posted there acknowledges nothing and blocks nothing — post them on the issue. #388.
- [packages/pg-js and the plain-JS examples have no formatter](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/227) — **decided in seven parts**, two of the ticket's three premises already dead. The style is a `prettier` key in `package.json` — the key is what halts prettier's upward search — duplicated into three packages rather than extracted. Execution is js#269.
- [the three stale reader rows: move pg-core to 0.6.5, pg-wasm to 0.6.5, pg-js to 2.4.0](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/379) — **shipped.** Rows move to pg-core 0.6.5, pg-wasm 0.6.5, pg-js 2.4.0, each a **replacement** — `no_two_pinned_readers_share_a_minor_line` will not resolve two `=` pins on one line. Expected stale again within days, which is e2e#50's argument.
- [pg-pkg: postguard_clients' 64-version cap is one budget for the whole fleet](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/388) — **shipped.** One `client_version` budget per client, keyed on the post-allowlist `client`, so cardinality is bounded at 8 x 64 rather than handing an attacker a fresh budget per invented name. Discharges the made-and-never-applied entry.
- [cryptify: move the four upload limits and the rolling window into config, and serve GET /limits](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/386) — **shipped**, `#344`'s server half. `fn limits(config: &State<CryptifyConfig>)` takes **only** config — nothing that can vary the body by `Authorization` — so caller-invariance is structural rather than merely tested.
- [compat: a crates.io backend, and a scheduled check that postguard's reader rows are current](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-e2e/issues/50) — **shipped, both halves**: a crates.io backend plus `check-reader-rows.mjs` on `compat-bump.yml`'s cron. The workflow half was handed over correctly and **never applied** — so checking the URL is not enough; the file has to be read.
- [fixtures: forward-direction job — HEAD-sealed artifacts opened by published readers](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-e2e/issues/25) — **superseded, and the architecture was inverted** — the forward direction shipped in `postguard` as `pg-compat`, where the sealer already lives, so nothing crosses a repo boundary. Only a *write-only* change separates it from the archival gate.
- [Bump prod cryptify off 0.1.25 once a 0.1.29 image exists](https://github.com/privacybydesign/postguard-ops/issues/68) — **merged and applied**; prod runs `cryptify_image_tag = "0.1.29"`. The harvest matters more: that commit is the last green apply this repo has had, the next sat undeployed twelve days (ops#72). **"merged" is not a status this repo can be asked for.**
- [website: fetch cryptify's upload limits instead of baking them, and fail closed when the fetch fails](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/267) — the two `VITE_*` copies are gone and `GET /limits` is fetched, send disabled until it answers. **A ticket's list of consumers is a premise like a line number, and the one most likely to be short** — it named two of four.
- [prod has not applied since 2026-08-17: both Terraform halves fail on every push, silently](https://github.com/privacybydesign/postguard-ops/issues/72) — **prod applies again**, and **both causes named in the ticket were misdiagnosed**. A run with zero steps still has an annotation stating the cause. Sharpest input for `ops#36`: the signal was *nothing has deployed*, not *a deploy failed*.
- [formatter for `packages/pg-js` and the two plain-JS examples, and the fail-open examples Lint step](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/269) — prettier shipped as `#227` decided; **the workflow half did not, and the guard built to catch it missed it** — `ci-wiring.test.ts` asserts jobs and contexts, not steps inside them. After any handover, read the file on `main`.
- [COMPATIBILITY.md: the 1.x retirement condition rests on telemetry that cannot see 1.x](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/382) — the document no longer promises a retirement test the metric cannot run. **A body's citations rot, and closing an issue is exactly what makes a reference to it wrong** — so `Verify before you build` has to point at an issue body's links too.
- [critical OpenSSL CVE in the Debian base blocks the release; the vulnerable path is unreachable from our binaries](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/394) — DSA-6465-1 is out of both images, the fix merged **before** the release PR. **Image package currency was pinned to the last time someone edited a Dockerfile** — two mechanisms, each concealing the other.
- [fixtures: a direct push to main bypasses the merge-base gate, leaving only the nightly ledger](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-e2e/issues/37) — **shipped**: `e2e.yml` gained `push` on `fixtures/**`, so a direct push rewriting a fixture and its ledger together is no longer caught a day late. The premise dissolved — `append-only.mjs` already reduces any ref with `git merge-base`.
- [fixtures: append-only corpus — every readable container format and envelope tier, tested in both directions](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-e2e/issues/19) — umbrella, **all five children done**, found open-but-done. Its `blocked by` edge to the last child was missing: edges are wired when an umbrella is charted, and nothing re-adds them for children filed later.
- [correct #310's scrape README to push-based Alloy and to the hostnames that exist, then merge it](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/370) — **shipped**, the **seventh dispatch**. On a map this old **gate 2 is answered in comments far more often than in bodies**: the first firing swept the body and missed two comments that had ruled it undispatchable twice.
- [the map body hit GitHub's 256 KiB cap and the Notes section had become a store](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/396) — narrative archived verbatim to three comments, Notes cut to standing rules (112,747 -> 15,430) and the body to 109,521 bytes; membership moved off the 100-cap sub-issue tree onto a `wayfinder:247` label. Superseded by #442.
- [the rolling-limit 413 discloses a claimed sender's used_bytes and resets_at, reopening the GHSA usage oracle through finalize](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/387) — **shipped**: `used_bytes` means the same on both 413 arms, `resets_at` on neither. **The gate chose the shape, not the code** — oasdiff at `fail-on: WARN` made a structural removal a workflow handover.
- [cryptify charges uploads to a claimed sender's rolling quota, so any address can be locked out of sending for 14 days](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/402) — **shipped**: the ledger is namespaced by what authority stood behind the key — `api-key:`, `proven:`, `unproven:` — and the check sums only its own. Requiring a proof was rejected: it would be a flag day.
- [a flaky proof test was really cryptify acknowledging a chunk PUT before its bytes were written](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/399) — **shipped**, the **tenth dispatch**: one awaited `file.flush()` after `write_all`. **The load-bearing part is not the race** — the durable row advanced while bytes were unwritten, which needs no scheduling luck. Gate replaced by #409.
- [commits landing while a release PR is open ship inside it but reach no changelog, ever](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/411) — **decided: detect, not prevent.** A full-history sweep found exactly two under-reporting tags. **Subset, not equality** — `pg-pkg-v0.6.0` carries 19 entries for 16 commits, so an equality check reds a correct release. Execution is #412.
- [the chunk-durability gate added with the fix fails open ~14 runs in 15](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/409) — **decided: make it unrepresentable, not detectable**, and two of three candidates turned out not to exist. **A mutation check that reports 1-in-15 is a failed mutation check, not a caveated pass.** Execution #415; #416 graduated.
- [changelog coverage: assert a released tag's entry lists every commit the tag contains](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/412) — **shipped**, the first workflow handover to complete at *both* ends since `#272`/`#324`, because it inverted the failure: the assertion was **red until the patch applied**. A merged PR with no `Closes` trailer leaves its ticket open.
- [cryptify: make an unflushed chunk write unrepresentable, and replace the gate that fails open](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/415) — **shipped**: `OpenOptions` is gone from `main.rs`, so `UploadFile` owns opening as well as writing — a wrapper you can bypass is a convention. The mutation bar was met as numbers: 20/20 red mutated, 20/20 green intact.
- [@e4a/pg-wasm publishes on every pg-core release and its changelog stopped at 0.5.5](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/413) — **decided: inherit with a pointer, not a per-version record.** **A measurement taken to size a decision can invalidate the decision** — the backfill count showed 8 of 10 entries would be pointer-only. Execution #419; npm listing spun out as #420.
- [guard postguard-js's 20 required contexts against its ruleset (the other half of #318)](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/331) — **decided: each repo guards its own ruleset, reds *and* files, and the 20 names move into `.github/required-rules.json`.** The **token boundary** decided it: a `postguard` job can read `postguard-js`'s ruleset but cannot file into it.
- [pg-wasm: make the changelog a pointer to pg-core's, and pin the premise that makes it true](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/419) — **shipped**, and the one that found a hole in the dispatch gate: an agent deleted 41 lines of history while passing all five acceptance checks. **A ticket that tells an agent to leave something alone needs a check that fails when it does not.**
- [@e4a/pg-wasm's npm listing is blank: no README, no changelog, manifest written by a workflow heredoc](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/420) — **all five questions settled**; execution is #427. One README that *ships*, a committed manifest, a pre-publish check with an offline self-test, no `files` field. **A published artifact makes its own permanent fixture.**
- [changelog-coverage reds on a real finding and files nothing: the reporting step has no test](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/425) — **decided: extract the reporting loop into a script, and gate the shape** (#429). `set +e` manages a shell you do not control; a bare script invocation makes the hazard stop existing. **Stub the effect, not the collaborator.**
- [#411 priced prevention out on a five-day window; the real exposure is one release-plz-pr run](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/426) — **decided: delete the window instead of guarding the merge** (#430) — **and overturned by #436**, which measured the saving at ~22s rather than ~8.5 minutes. **A cost that decided a question is a premise like any other.**
- [the Safari wasm leg timed out on main and nothing noticed](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/416) — **decided: the leg stays, the retry wrapper goes, the budget becomes honest**; execution #432. Three of four premises were wrong — the cost was a **median 5m14s**, not twenty minutes, and the ~22-minute shape is safari-only.
- [pg-wasm: ship the README, commit the manifest, and refuse to publish an assembled package missing either](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/427) — **shipped**, the first workflow handover in this repo verified end to end rather than reported — both files read on `main` and the step's own output read from a run there. **Assert the order, not just the presence.**
- [release-plz recomputes a semver check the required gate already ran](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/430) — **shipped** — and it removed ~22s of the ~8.5 minutes it was scoped to remove; the setting and its gate are sound, #426's cost attribution was not, and the window is still ~5m46s -> #436.
- [changelog-coverage: move the reporting loop out of YAML, and gate the shape that broke it](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/429) — **shipped**, all four of #425's decisions intact. **The handover completed at both ends by construction, not luck**: the RED assertions made the patch unmergeable unapplied, so the workflow half arrived on the PR branch before merge.
- [pg-js forwards caller headers meant for Cryptify to the PKG, failing its CORS preflight](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/275) — **shipped**: `cryptifyChannel` on `PostGuardConfig`. The **client** half of a two-repo fix whose server half (#437) shipped separately — neither repo's tests can see the seam, which is the audit's thesis in one incident.
- [the release-plz-pr window is still ~5m46s: 312 of 327 seconds are unlogged, and semver_check was not the cost](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/436) — **decided: the window is irreducible, so #426 is overturned and the merge gets guarded** (#441). **A silent log is evidence about logging, not about work** — the step emits 507 `Compiling` lines release-plz does not forward.
- [wasm browser job: an honest timeout, no retry wrapper, and ci_wiring pins so the patch cannot be unapplied](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/432) — **shipped**, all three legs green on `main` at the **step output** rather than the check mark. The handover's second instance: RED assertions, maintainer patch applied onto the branch before merge.
- [guard main's required rules from this repo: extract the 20 contexts, read the live ruleset, file on drift](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/274) — **shipped**, closing the Notes' standing gap that `postguard-js`'s 20 contexts were unguarded (#331). **A third failure mode for the handover class**: the patch was posted twice and only the base64 copy carried the fix.
- [postguard's ruleset-drift job reds on drift and files nothing](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/422) — **built** (#443): the gate now files a `ruleset-drift` issue on exit 1, push-to-`main` only; exit 2 still reds and files nothing. Verified in a run on `main`. #443 sat green and in draft for 11 days — the fifth dispatch to lose only `gh pr ready`.
- [the map body is 9 KB over its own budget: Decisions-so-far is 109 entries in 132 KB, and #396's rule never covered it](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/442) — **rewritten 164,444 -> 67,958 bytes**, every entry now <=400. 31 entries verified against their tickets first: 25 fully duplicate, ~3.2 KB unique. #419 had no resolution comment, backfilled there. Checker is #445.

## Not yet specified

<!-- in-scope fog: real, coming, not yet sharp enough to ticket -->

- **Whether the fleet converges on one issue-filing idiom, or accepts per-repo shapes.** Four filing blocks now exist or are being built and no two agree: `delivery.yml`'s (extracted to a script by [#429](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/429)); [#422](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/422)'s, which copies #429 and adds a `push`-to-`main` guard the others lack; [postguard-js#274](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard-js/issues/274)'s, dispatched with an inline `set +e` in YAML; and `postguard-js`'s existing `sdk-canary.yml`, which *comments on* an existing issue rather than skipping, and captures no exit code at all because it is a separate `failure()`-gated job. **It now has a named consumer waiting on it**: [#416](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/416) decided the wasm browser job needs a voice when it reds on `main`, established that #429's script is changelog-specific rather than a reusable filer, and deliberately shipped [#432](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/432) without a fifth block — so `test-wasm-browsers` stays silent until this resolves, and that silence is a known debt, not an oversight. **Not yet a ticket because the sharp question cannot be phrased until #274 lands** — until then there is nothing to price the divergence against, and #425 deliberately declined to pull a dispatched ticket back for style. One sharp thing to carry into it: `sdk-canary.yml`'s `existing=$(gh issue list ...)` dedupe read is a **line-111 twin**, the same abort under `bash -e {0}`, untouched and in another repo where #429's `ci_wiring.rs` assertion cannot see it.
- **Which routes, fields, and headers actually get removed under `#257`, and when.** Collection is [ops#70](https://github.com/privacybydesign/postguard-ops/issues/70)/[ops#71](https://github.com/privacybydesign/postguard-ops/issues/71). [#371](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/371) **narrowed this patch rather than clearing it, and inverted what it is waiting on.** The earlier note here said the data was unreadable as a deprecation signal until `#371` added an `unknown` bucket; that is wrong, and the bucket does not make it readable. The split to carry: the `path` label is bounded by the server's own route table, so **route**-level removal *is* answerable once scraping runs — but no measurement distinguishes one client **version** from another when the client does not send the header, so that half waits on nothing and is an announcement plus a window, not a metric. Split it that way when it graduates rather than filing one ticket that half-can-be-answered.
- **What reaches Cockpit Loki, and what `log_format` prod should run instead.** Opened by `ops#72` decision 1: Cockpit log shipping *is* wanted in prod, and `ops#73` leaves the Alloy blocks written and switched off behind two absent credentials, so turning it on is now a two-secret operation with no code change — which is exactly why the question has to be answered before someone does it. The procolix vhost sets no `access_log`, so nginx's default `combined` format applies and logs `$remote_addr` plus the full `$request`; cryptify's routes are `GET /usage?<email>`, `/fileupload/<uuid>`, `/fileupload/<uuid>/status` and `/filedownload/<filename>`. So the default arrangement ships client IPs, recipient email addresses and download references to a third-party log store — the same identifier set `apps/website/src/lib/reportScrub.ts` exists to strip out of Sentry. Not yet a ticket because the sharp question is which `log_format` (or which redacting `map`) prod should run, not whether the pipeline should exist. **And nginx is not the only sink.** `cryptify`'s own application log writes the accounting key — since [#402](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/402) a namespaced `unproven:`/`proven:`/`api-key:` key, so still the canonicalized *claimed* sender email on the default tier — together with that address's 14-day `used_bytes`, at `info`, on **every** finalize: the `log::info!` above the rolling-limit check in `upload_finalize`. Found while resolving [#387](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/387) and deliberately left there, because changing what an operational log line says is a judgement about diagnostic value and belongs to this decision rather than to a security fix. So the question is which format **and which application log lines**, with two code owners rather than one — settling the nginx half alone would ship the same identifier set from a different file and read as done.
- **What replaces SonarQube**, if `#48` resolves as "remove" rather than "fix".
- **Whether the Safari wasm leg has one failure mode or two.** [#416](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/416) characterised it as zero `… ok` lines and ~17 minutes of silence, and that diagnosis is what [#432](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/issues/432) was built against. On 2026-09-22 it failed the other way on [#443](https://github.com/encryption4all/postguard/pull/443): **8 of 16 tests completed**, then `Failed to detect test as having been run` 26s after `running 16 tests`, whole job 5m25s. #432's timeout worked — five minutes, not twenty-two — but a reader matching on #416's signature will not recognise this. **Not a ticket at n=1**: a re-run passed and the identical tree passed Safari on the previous sha, so the sharp question (distinct fault, or the same one now caught early?) needs a second occurrence. Recorded on #416.

## Out of scope

<!-- ruled beyond the destination; never graduates -->

- **An RFC, a protocol registry, or capability negotiation.** The audit's central negative finding: it would have prevented **zero** of the year's ~60 incidents. Recorded here so it is not re-litigated — executable contracts are the answer instead.
- **Product bugs the audit surfaced but deliberately tracks in place**, not as children of this map: `#197`, the mobile Yivi cluster (`postguard-website#264`/`#270`/`#271`/`#272`), `cryptify#47`, `postguard-website#280`.
- **The superseded programme:** EPIC `#201` and its phases `#202`/`#208`/`#213`/`#214`/`#215`, closed when this epic replaced them. Its phases 0–3 delivered the harness, the pinned contracts, and the drift detector that this map builds on.
- **Zeroizing USK/MSK on drop in `pg-core`.** A known-open security gap (no `zeroize` dependency yet), but never part of the audit's remediation set and never a child here. Needs its own effort.
